Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a routine inspection of wells in the area. At the time of this inspection it is approximately 50 degrees with light rain falling. The “main” artery into the area has accelerated erosion channels, most notably in the vicinity of the M Bailie 89 Well (003-21925) and Gaston 1 Well (003-21967). The Department recommends that the operator maintain the access road to correct and prevent further accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues. Operator representative Isaac Haky was advised via phone of noted deficiencies. The site appears to be constructed and the well appears equipped for production. There is a single plastic Production Tank on site. No leaks, spills, dead or dying vegetation observed. There is a posted Information Placard on a piece of production equipment. The Department spoke with Isaac, a representative of the operator who told us that labels would be affixed to the well head in accordance with regulations as soon as possible. Based on this inspection violations are being issued for the observed accelerated erosion on the access road.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 8/31/2022
Violation Code: 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.

Permit API: 059-23883
Unconventional: No
County: Greene
Municipality: Greene Twp

Inspection Date: 8/31/2022
Comments: On 8/31 a routine complete inspection of the Kemsod 1 OG Well was conducted.During the inspection the following was observed:-A well tag was present on the wellhead (Photo #2). A greasy residue was obstructing the numbers on the well tag. It appeared to have dripped from the joint above the tag. -Operator and well information was present and visible at the wellsite (Photo #3).-The production tank appeared to be in generally good condition. No berm was present around the tank (Photo #4).-A trailer was observed next to the tank (Photos #1 and #5). A thick greasy substance was present on the trailer (Photos #6, #7, #8 and #10). The substance appeared to have slowly dripped from the trailer along the side (Photos # #8, #9, and #11). No active dripping was observed.Violation of 78.56(a) is being issued for failure to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks. Violation of 78.55 (a) is being issued for failure to implement a waste control and disposal plan under 91.34 (relating to activities utilizing pollutants) for the control and disposal of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, additives, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, production fluids and drill cuttings from the drilling, alteration, production, plugging or other activity associated with oil and gas wells.Violation of 91.34(a) is being issued for failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.Violation of 78.66(e) is being issued for recover or remove the substance which was released.

Violation ID: 845827
Permit API: 047-23756
Unconventional: No
County: Elk
Municipality: Saint Marys City
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-04-02
Comments: This inspection was performed following a report to the NWRO by Diversified Oil and Gas of a 25 gallon brine spill at their #38067 well. It appears as though a small leak formed in a 50 barrel poly tank over the winter, which allowed some production fluid to leach out slowly over time. Once the snow melted, the well tender noticed a small area (~10x10 ft) that had vegetation missing and deer prints. The diking was unlined, so it seems that production water had leached out, and high conductivity levels were noted in this area. All the brine stayed in a small area, and no waters are nearby to be a concern for migration. The operator has shut in this well for the time being, and excavation is scheduled for the week of 4/8. Continued inspection of this site will be performed at that time.

Comments: On 6/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Solowiej well site. It was 65 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. I did not screen for conductivity because I did not witness any water puddles or muddy areas on the pad surface during the inspection.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by one sediment pond. The sediment pond is adequately stabilized and was dry at the time of the inspection. I was able to witness an 8 inch riser sticking up about 16 inches from the pond surface. The outlet for the sediment pond overflow drains into a stream alongside the River View roadway. This stream drains to the waters of the Commonwealth. Following an inspection conducted on 10/18/2022, Chesapeake reported that it would make changes to the site to mitigate the issues with the sediment pond. They reported that they were developing a design to accommodate both the drainage and the land owner and hoped to have a finalized plan with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features. There are outstanding violations against the outfall coming off the sediment pond. There were three wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake continues with the process to obtain a revised ESCGP application with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features and submit to the Department for review.I left the site at 1400 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/19/2026 to K PETROLEUM INC in Somerset Township, Washington county. 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect  brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect brine and other fluids produced during operation of the well in a tank, series of tanks, or other device approved by the Department for subsequent disposal or reuse.
Violation ID: 8286049
Permit API: 125-23924
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/19/2026
Comments: On August 19, 2026, the Department conducted a complaint inspection of the Cecil 2-P229 OG Well in regard to CTS 400392.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.At the time of the inspection the well was located in an open agricultural field. The access road appeared stabilized. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed at the time of the inspection.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting were present onsite appeared to have all information in accordance with OGA3211(G) and OGA3211(H). There were no observed leaks or discharges of fluid at the surface around the wellhead.There appeared to be 3 total production tanks onsite. Upon further inspection, it appeared the white poly tank was connected and in use. The tank appeared to be in sound condition with no observed leaks or discharges of fluid were observed around this tank.Two metal tanks were also present onsite but did not appear to be in use at the time of the inspection. Upon further inspection of the 2 metal tanks, one of the tanks appeared to be severely corroded with multiple holes in the tank observed. The Department observed fluid flowing down the side of the tank. A conductivity reading of this fluid was obtained and was "OR" (Over detectable range, >20mS). Upon inspection of the ground surrounding the corroded production tank, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of staining and saturation with readings of 12.78mS, 9.24mS, 4.37mS, and 1.82mS being obtained. These readings are elevated in comparison to the background conductivity reading obtained of 0.19mS. Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings, it appears a release has/is occurring from the corroded production tank.Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and informed him of the Department's observations of an apparent release. Mr. Inghram stated the metal tanks have been disconnected and empty for several years. The Department recommended remediation of the spill and removal of the production tanks as they are no longer in use and heavily corroded. Mr. Inghram stated he would get a contractor to begin the work as soon as possible.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite.

An Act 9 sign and well permits are posted at the site entrance (photo #1).No standing water was observed on the pad surface.The Patterson 582 drilling rig is noted onsite; the Ron 3UH well has been drilled and the rig is currently drilling the Ron 4UH well, the Ron 5UH has yet to be drilled (photo #2). The GPUs are stationed in a secondary containment structure which held less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #7); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed (photos #11 and 12). 1 infiltration basins serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #13). Comments: On September 18, 2024 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well Site located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3774486 where violations were issued for an 18-20 barrel release of production fluid from a production tank on June 4, 2024.At the time of this inspection, the access road appeared stabilized with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed and the production tank that was leaking during IR 3774486 has since been removed from the well site. A well tag was fixed to the wellhead with all required information posted on it, and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed coming from or near the wellhead. The area where the production tank once (where the spill originated), the slope that the spill traveled down, and the area downstream where the spill pooled up at now appears to be backfilled, seeded and mulched pending vegetative growth. In addition, at the edge of the downslope area right before a forested area began, some black fencing was observed.Several soil conductivity readings were taken in the spill areas (0.0418 mS, 0.0362 mS, 0.0054 mS, 0.0137 mS, and 0.0602 mS) and are significantly lower than the soil conductivity readings taken in the same areas at the time of the spill (Soil conductivity readings taken on 6/4/24 documented in IR 3774486: 1.35 mS, 1.454 mS, Over Range, 7.63 mS, 5.51 mS, and 4.90 mS). Upon inspection of the fence, two areas appeared to be compromised. A stake appeared to be snapped and the fence appeared to be pushed down by sediment, at this time, there did not appear to be any evidence of the sediment overtopping the fence and no erosion or sedimentation was observed behind this section of fence. Another section of the fence right behind a small tree appeared to not be trenched and a gap was observed between the bottom of the fence and the ground. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed behind this section of the fence a this time either.The Department is recommending the Operator promptly properly implement and maintain the temporary erosion and sedimentation (E and S) best management practices (BMPs) to prevent any pollution from occurring.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain E and S BMPs. In addition, violations issued during IR 3774486 shall remain outstanding until the Act 2 Report is submitted, received, reviewed and approved by the Environmental Cleanup and Brownfields (ECB) Program.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Eqt Prod Co

Violation Date: 2019-03-15
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 844756
Permit API: 003-22404
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Forward Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-03-15
Comments: On-site inspection conducted in response to a release of 35 gallons impaired water reported under inspection record 2856634. At the time of this inspection, fracturing operations are ongoing. After arriving on-site, the Department contacted operator representative DJ Hardy by phone at 1316. Per Mr. Hardy, a pump failed during the frac and the transfer line overflowed, resulting in a release of 50 bbl frac water with 35 gallons off of containment. It is believed there is a hole in the containment that allowed this impaired water to be released outside of containment although that hole has yet to be identified. The containment was being pumped out this morning. Mr. Hardy did not respond to this release and will therefore have the appropriate Environmental contact call the Department. At 1335, Jim Noon (EQT Environmental Coordinator) contacted the Department by phone. Per Mr. Noon: Mr. Noon was at the site earlier this morning when the fluid was still being removed from the containment. The release occurred when a discharge hose froze, causing the blunder to overflow frac slurry onto containment before the water transfer could be shut down. It is possible the frac slurry traveled off of containment due to a hole in the containment or a tear in one of the seams; neither have been located at this time. The 35 gallons quantity provided was based off the quantity left in the line and also a visual estimation. Operator representative Darin Sweeney showed the Department where the release occurred. It appears that residual frac slurry/impaired water remains on the containment and also off of containment, notably on the outside edges of the containment. The Department recommends the operator remove all contaminated materials as soon as possible and continue implementing the PPC plan as outlined. Violations are being issued for this reportable release.

Inspection Date: 2020-02-06
Comments: Arrived onsite at 10:31 in response to a reported release of 15 gallons of glycol from a compressor. I talked with Kellon Balum, Chief, during the inspection. He indicated that free liquid had be removed with a vac truck the previous evening. Equipment was also brought in to remove any visually impacted soil. About 10 cubic yards of soil was removed. After the compressor was brought back online, some remaining glycol left the containment and collected with water in a small sump that was dug near the compressor. A vac truck was brought back to continue to remove the water from the sump as needed. No other issues were noted at the site. All secondary containment appeared to be in good condition and free from excess water. The wells were properly tagged and the cellars filled in with gravel. The site was greater than 70% vegetative cover and appeared stable. It is recommended that the small area of the sump be excavated after no additional glycol collects. The area can then be backfilled and the residual waste disposed of properly. The DEP acknowledges the proper reporting and prompt remediation of the release. The result of this inspection is Violations Noted & Immediately Corrected.

Comments: On 9/27/2022, DEP representatives John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Hopson well site. Assess the area noted with high conductance water on the fill slope and provide immediate protection as necessary to prevent pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.2. Assess the rock area where the sample was collected for the extent of contamination and report/respond accordingly. Include the contaminated area in the site Act 2 response.

Report Details

Violation ID: 847372
Permit API: 031-25096
Unconventional: No
County: Clarion
Municipality: Piney Twp

Inspection Date: 2019-04-16
Comments: An oil release to ground from a malfunctioning valve on the discharge pipe of one of the two tanks located in secondary containment at this well site was reported by Kenneth Fleeman on April 11, 2019. Oil was released from the tank by a malfunctioning valve which resulted in oil flow to the southwest end of the secondary containment where it disappeared into the stony soil. There is dead vegetation and oily pools of water observed to the east, south and west of the secondary containment. A 200 foot path of dead vegetation extends south of the well site. The path of dead vegetation disappears on the slope south of the well site and does not appear to have reached any waterways. A patch of dead vegetation and several oily pools of water is evident 15' east of the secondary containment. There is a 50' to 70' path of vegetation to the southwest however the oil does not appear to have moved any farther. Abarta Production Supervisor, Scott Patterson, stated that all tanks and piping were intact at the time of his inspection of the well on April 1, 2019 and the tank had approximately 13" of oil (10.75 barrels) at that time. All oil above the the discharge pipe was released to ground. Based on conductivity testing this was an oil release only, no brine was released. This is a violation of PA Oil and Gas Regulations and a clean-up process will be required. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 800-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil &Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-12-23 to Diversified Oil & Gas Llc in Cumberland Twp, Greene county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Diversified Oil & Gas Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-12-23
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 872392
Permit API: 059-24428
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Cumberland Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-23
Comments: On 12/19/19 a malfunction with the GPU occurred, causing the vessel to explode. On 12/20/19 OGI Joel Keller conducted inspection 2974755 and noted soil staining and a damp appearance. OGI Keller requested a follow up inspection be conducted by a WQS. On 12/23/19 at approximately 0800 I conducted a follow up inspection. The temperature was well below freezing at the time of inspection. Upon arriving at the explosion location I observed water on the access road that was not frozen, despite the freezing temperature. A soil conductivity probe was utilized and a reading od 12.02mS was observed (see photograph). Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed throughout the access road and on the east side of the access road. Trees and shrubs on the east side of the access road appeared wet. The liquid was not frozen and appeared to be brine, as further demonstrated by elevated soil conductivity readings in the area. No other trees or shrubs appeared wet, except for those east of the GPU location where elevated soil conductivity was observed. Additional elevated soil conductivity readings were observed further North toward the well head on the east side of the access road (see photographs). Elevated soil conductivity readings were also observed adjacent to brine tank 2. The highest reading observed was 12.83mS. Both brine tanks were severely corroded and brine tank 2 exhibited a large hole (see photographs). Brine tank 1 exhibited several smaller holes that appeared to have occurred due to shrapnel from the GPU explosion. The gravel in the former GPU location appeared to be stained, but the soil conductivity was not elevated. The Department recommends the visually impacted material is removed. Soil sample 3402-076 was collected from an area exhibiting elevated soil conductivity. Soil sample 3402-077 was collected from an area on the northwest portion of the site in an area that appeared to be unimpaired with low notably lower soil conductivity (see photographs). The Department recommends the spill is addressed consistent with the Act 2 process.

Comments: The Department conducted a follow up inspection of this well on 11/14/2023. The well was located in an open and mowed lawn at the end of a dead end street. The well was not tagged or labeled. The well was equipped to produce gas off the production casing, and the valves at the well head were in the open position. A gauge installed at the well read 20psi. The Department spoke the landowner and was informed that the well supplies gas to the house and is used as a heating source. Gas was not observed venting from the backside of the production casing, however gas was observed leaking from the production casing swage at the time of the inspection. Production and MIA reports have not been received by the Department. The violation of 78.121(A) remains outstanding. New violations and outstanding violations are noted.
